canon.rule: A Pokémon never speaks human words — it says its own name and nothing else, in a hundred different tones that its trainer learns to read exactly.
The one famous exception is Team Rocket's Meowth, who taught himself human speech the hard way and will tell anyone about it.
Pokémon understand their trainers perfectly well even though they cannot answer, and a well-bonded pair needs barely a word to act together.
A Pokémon is caught by weakening it in a fair battle and then throwing a Poké Ball, and a Pokémon that does not want to be caught can break straight back out.
A trainer carries at most six Pokémon at a time, and the rest wait safely elsewhere.
A battle ends when a Pokémon faints — never worse than that — and a fainted Pokémon is healed completely at any Pokémon Center, free, usually within the hour.

Every Pokémon and every move has a type, and type decides the battle: water beats fire, fire beats grass, grass beats water, electric beats water and flying, ground beats electric, and rock beats flying and fire.
A move of a type the target resists barely lands at all, and an electric attack does nothing whatsoever to a ground-type Pokémon.

Many Pokémon evolve into a bigger, stronger form with experience — Charmander to Charmeleon to Charizard, Bulbasaur to Ivysaur to Venusaur, Squirtle to Wartortle to Blastoise — and an evolution is permanent.

Eevee is the exception that evolves eight different ways depending on how it is raised — Vaporeon by a Water Stone, Jolteon by a Thunder Stone, Flareon by a Fire Stone, Espeon and Umbreon through friendship by day or by night, Leafeon and Glaceon near a mossy or an icy rock, and Sylveon through affection and a fairy-type move.
A Pokémon knows only four moves at a time, and teaching it a fifth means giving one up.
A Pokédex identifies any Pokémon on sight and reads out its entry, whether or not anyone asked it to.
Gyms are run by Gym Leaders who each specialise in one type, and beating one earns a badge; eight badges get a trainer into the League.
Legendary Pokémon are one of a kind, enormously powerful, and almost never caught — meeting one at all is the story.
Charizard's tail flame is its life — if that flame ever went out, so would Charizard — so it is never let near heavy rain unguarded.
Team Rocket's schemes always fail, always end with the three of them launched into the sky, and never actually hurt anyone.

characters.name: Pikachu
characters.role: the best-known Pokémon in the world, an Electric-type and the model of a bonded partner
characters.status: alive and well, riding on its trainer's shoulder
characters.physical: small and yellow with a lightning-bolt tail, long black-tipped ears and round red cheek pouches that spark before an attack
characters.voice: does not speak — says 'Pika', 'Pika-pi' and 'Chuuu' with a hundred meanings, and sparks its cheeks when it means business
characters.motivation: its trainer, ketchup, and never being put in a Poké Ball
possessions: nothing — it refuses to be carried in a ball
knows: Thunderbolt, Quick Attack, Iron Tail and Electro Ball
does_not_know: how to hold back when its friends are threatened

characters.name: Nurse Joy
characters.role: the nurse who runs the Pokémon Center in every town
characters.physical: in a pink nurse's uniform with a white apron and looped pink hair under a white cap
characters.voice: unfailingly gentle and professional — 'we've restored your Pokémon to full health, we hope to see you again!' — and completely unflappable no matter what walks through the door
characters.motivation: every Pokémon that comes through her doors leaving healthy
possessions: the healing machine behind her counter
knows: how to treat any Pokémon of any type
does_not_know: why trainers keep apologising for bringing her work

characters.name: Jessie
characters.role: one third of the Team Rocket trio who chase rare Pokémon and never catch one
characters.status: alive and well, hiding in a bush
characters.physical: tall with an enormous swept curl of magenta hair, in a white Team Rocket uniform with a red R
characters.voice: theatrical and imperious, delivers half of a rhyming motto at full volume, and turns on a coin from grand villain to howling sulk
characters.motivation: one great catch that finally impresses the boss
possessions: a balloon shaped like a Meowth
does_not_know: that the plan will not work

characters.name: James
characters.role: the second of the Team Rocket trio
characters.status: alive and well, in the same bush
characters.physical: with short lavender hair, in a white Team Rocket uniform with a red R
characters.voice: delivers the other half of the motto with as much drama as Jessie, agrees with whatever she just said, and goes soft and sentimental about any Pokémon he meets
characters.motivation: sticking with his friends, and one good catch
possessions: the other half of the disguises
does_not_know: how to say no to Jessie

characters.name: Meowth
characters.role: the talking Pokémon of the Team Rocket trio
characters.status: alive and well, doing all the thinking
characters.physical: a cream-coloured cat Pokémon walking upright, with a gold charm set in his forehead, whiskers and curled tail
characters.voice: speaks actual human words in a fast wisecracking city accent — the only Pokémon who does — and finishes the motto with 'Meowth, that's right!'
characters.motivation: proving a Pokémon who talks is worth more than one who battles
possessions: the plans, which he draws himself
knows: how to talk, which he taught himself
does_not_know: that the others could not manage without him

last_seen.location: behind the bush, holding a diagram

relationships.state: inseparable partners in every failed scheme, and each other's only real family
relationships.history: They have blasted off together more times than either can count and have never once considered splitting up.

relationships.state: constant bickering over whose plan it was, and complete loyalty underneath it
relationships.history: Meowth draws the plans, Jessie takes the credit, and neither would leave the other behind.

relationships.state: the one person on the road every trainer is glad to see
relationships.history: Every Center in every town is hers, and no trainer has ever been turned away.

locations.name: the Pokémon Center
locations.description: A red-roofed building in every town with a healing machine behind the counter, a phone to call home, and beds for trainers passing through
locations.state: open, free, and busy at all hours

locations.name: the town Gym
locations.description: A hall built around one battlefield and themed to its Leader's type — rock, water, electric — with a badge waiting for whoever wins
locations.state: open to any trainer who asks for a match

locations.name: the route between towns
locations.description: Long grass, forest paths and rivers where wild Pokémon appear without warning, and where most of a journey actually happens
locations.state: walked daily, and never quite the same twice
